newsitem.title: USA: Ford idles Taurus, Sable plants for one week.
newsitem.headline: Ford idles Taurus, Sable plants for one week.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Monday that it was idling production plants in Atlanta and Chicago, affecting 4,700 hourly workers, because of insufficient orders from dealers for Ford Taurus and Mercury Sable models.
The one-week shut down will idle 2,200 hourly workers in Atlanta and 2,500 in Chicago. Together the two plants produce about 10,800 Taurus and Sable cars weekly.
Ford said sales of the mainstay Taurus and Sable models had been hurt by aggressive price cuts by Japanese automakers, who have benefited by the weakness of the yen against the dollar.
Ford also said the currency situation has resulted in a sharp drop in Taurus export demand, primarily for Japan.

"As a result, there is an insufficient backlog of buildable dealer orders for Taurus and Sable to make up for the export decline and maintain production without interruption," Ford said in a statement.
Ford said at the end of February that its dealers had a 62-day supply of Tauruses and a 51-day supply of Sables.
The company also said that it may make a separate announcement later Monday about the future of its assembly plant in Lorain, Ohio, that makes Ford Thunderbirds and Mercury Cougars.
A Ford spokesman declined to elaborate on the nature of the announcement. "I can only say 'stay tuned,'" he said.
The automaker is expected to acknowledge that it will end production of Thunderbirds and Cougars at Lorain by the end of the year, and idle the plant's car assembly line.
A second assembly line at the factory, which produces Econoline full-size vans, will remain in operation.

Cougar production is expected to be shifted next year to a new car platform that will be built in Flat Rock, Mich., at AutoAlliance International Inc., Ford's U.S. joint venture with Mazda Motor Corp.
Ford's stock fell 50 cents to $31.625 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.

But Ford said the Thunderbird will be resurrected as a new speciality sports coupe "designed to draw from its early heritage when it was first introduced in 1954." It will be developed from "soon-to-be-launched, multi-vehicle platform" and built at an undisclosed site.

The shutdown of the Lorain car system, scheduled for the third quarter, will cause Ford to indefinitely idle about 2,500 employees, including 1,800 at the Lorain plant and up to 700 at Ford components plants elsewhere.
Production of Ford Econoline full-size vans, on a separate assembly line in the Lorain plant, will continue unaffected.
Aerostar production in St. Louis will end August 22, but Ford said the move will not affect employment there, because it plans to boost output of Explorer sport utility vehicles at the same plant.

Production of the Probe will end June 17 at the Auto Alliance International plant in Flat Rock, Mich., but employees at the Ford/Mazda Motor Corp. joint venture will begin building 1998 Mazda models in September. Auto Alliance also will build another Ford product in the future, but Ford officials declined to elaborate on it.
